original_test_intent: Verify that every firmware component's displayed version naming agrees across Redfish FirmwareInventory, the release note, firmware image/package filename and WebUI.
original_method: Collect each member through validated collection links, preserve raw identity/version values, load authenticated same-build external references and apply an approved component mapping and normalization rule without changing firmware.
manual_activity: Supply the release note, exact firmware package/image filenames and WebUI export or screenshots for the same build; approve component aliases and any non-semantic normalization rules.
required_inputs: Authoritative release note for the installed build
Exact firmware package/image manifest and filenames
WebUI version evidence for the same target
safety_requirements: No hardcoded credentials or unapproved TLS bypass
Use member URIs returned by the collection
Never normalize away digits, build identifiers or component identity
Do not compare artifacts from different builds
Report missing evidence separately from mismatch
agent_execution_scope: Hash and identify release-note and package artifacts
Emit raw and normalized per-component comparisons
Flag duplicates, missing mappings and exact mismatches

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It improves the malformed source path and gathers Redfish Name/Version, but collection `.Members[].Id` may not exist for link-only members, constructed IDs need validation, and no release-note/file/WebUI inputs make the acceptance decision possible.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Traverse validated member URIs over verified TLS, preserve raw values, load provenance-checked same-build external artifacts, then compare via an approved component map and lossless normalization table.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The all-firmware scope and 15/10 timing are retained; no component alias, release version, filename format or permitted normalization is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a four-surface reconciliation table keyed by stable component identity, with raw values, artifact provenance, explicit aliases and reversible normalization.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Corrects URI handling and adds the external oracles, provenance, component mapping and deterministic comparison needed by Criteria 3.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Validates displayed naming consistency only; it does not establish image compatibility, active-bank status, firmware function or update success.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: WebUI may use marketing aliases and filenames may encode package rather than component versions; those differences require documented mappings rather than ad hoc string stripping.

project_override_considerations: If one package contains several component images, compare each member to the manifest entry, not the outer archive filename. Preserve both active and backup inventory entries when present and do not conflate their roles.
expected_evidence: Approved component mapping and normalization rules
Normalized comparison and exact mismatch reason
No firmware update/reset and preserved logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure, Criteria and Script consistently require per-component FirmwareInventory reads and cross-surface version naming comparison. The source command is malformed and incomplete but does not contradict that goal.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The missing release artifacts, WebUI evidence, mapping and normalization rules are identifiable project inputs, so the case is REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Changes a Redfish-only value dump into a provenance-backed, component-specific reconciliation that can actually decide the named release/file/WebUI synchronization criterion.
independent_technical_reasoning: Version strings are not safely comparable without first establishing component identity and build provenance. A BMC active image, backup bank, CPLD and host BIOS can use different prefixes or build suffixes, while an outer firmware bundle filename may describe the bundle rather than any one member. Normalization must therefore be documented and lossless with respect to semantic digits and bank role. Exact raw values remain evidence so a reported match can be audited and an alias cannot conceal a genuine release mismatch.
